readings: Group the Examination table by ID, so only IDs that have at least one Examination record are included. Count the records per ID and divide each count by the total number of Examination records to get its share. The average share is the mean of these shares across those IDs. Keep the IDs whose share is strictly above that average. For those IDs, return one unrounded row with their average record count, their average share, and the average of (share minus the average share).

Start from every patient in the Patient table, so patients with no Examination records are included with a count of 0. Count the Examination records per patient ID and divide each count by the total number of Examination records to get its share. The average share is the mean of these shares across all patients. Keep the IDs whose share is strictly above that average. For those IDs, return one unrounded row with their average record count, their average share, and the average of (share minus the average share).
queries:
WITH counts AS (
    SELECT ID, COUNT(*) AS cnt
    FROM Examination
    GROUP BY ID
),
total AS (
    SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_cnt FROM Examination
),
shares AS (
    SELECT c.ID, c.cnt, CAST(c.cnt AS REAL) / t.total_cnt AS share
    FROM counts c, total t
),
avg_share AS (
    SELECT AVG(share) AS a FROM shares
)
SELECT AVG(s.cnt) AS avg_count,
       AVG(s.share) AS avg_share,
       AVG(s.share - a.a) AS avg_diff
FROM shares s, avg_share a
WHERE s.share > a.a;
WITH counts AS (
    SELECT p.ID AS ID, COUNT(e.ID) AS cnt
    FROM Patient p
    LEFT JOIN Examination e ON e.ID = p.ID
    GROUP BY p.ID
),
total AS (
    SELECT CAST(SUM(cnt) AS REAL) AS t FROM counts
),
shares AS (
    SELECT c.ID, c.cnt, c.cnt / total.t AS share
    FROM counts c, total
),
avg_share AS (
    SELECT AVG(share) AS a FROM shares
)
SELECT AVG(s.cnt) AS avg_count,
       AVG(s.share) AS avg_share,
       AVG(s.share - avg_share.a) AS avg_diff
FROM shares s, avg_share
WHERE s.share > avg_share.a;
